title: Scrum Sprint Board
description: Epics, stories, sprints with points rollups, ceremonies and retrospectives.
forWho: Scrum teams in software or game studios

spec.useCase: Isolde Varga is scrum master at a small game studio and uses this to run sprint planning, see velocity and keep retrospective actions from being forgotten.

business.name: Lumenhaus Games
business.describes: An independent studio making a puzzle-adventure game about a lighthouse keeper.

tables.name: Epics
tables.describes: Large pieces of the game, each made of stories, with points rolled up.
tables.subject: thing

independentOf.stories: The two sides move on their own schedule and status; neither forces the other.

tables.name: Sprints
tables.describes: Two-week sprints with a goal, capacity and the points committed and completed.
tables.subject: thing

values.goal: Players can light and carry a lantern
The harbor level is walkable end to end
Tides change the paths in the harbor
Ambient creatures and first audio pass

independentOf.stories: The two sides move on their own schedule and status; neither forces the other.

tables.name: Stories
tables.describes: Every story, bug and task, its points, who has it and whether it is blocked.
tables.subject: thing

values.title: Lantern oil meter in the HUD
Tide height curve over a day
Paths appear and vanish with the tide
Crash on loading a very old save
Gull flocks that follow the player

independentOf.assignee: Anyone can pick up a story.

tables.name: Retrospectives
tables.describes: What the team learned at the end of each sprint and who follows up.
tables.subject: thing

values.went_well: Lantern shader landed early; pairing on tricky bugs helped.
values.to_improve: Estimates for the pipeline task were far too low.

values.went_well: The harbor tilemap was done a day ahead; design and code stayed in sync.
values.to_improve: Review queue backed up on Thursday.

values.went_well: Water and tide work came together faster than planned.
values.to_improve: The very old save crash ate two days; we need a save-format test.

independentOf.sprint: The two sides move on their own schedule and status; neither forces the other.

relationships.describes: An epic is made of stories.
A sprint holds the stories the team committed to.

forms.name: Propose a story
forms.describes: How anyone on the team adds a story to the backlog.

fields.ask: What should the player or team be able to do?
Is it a story, a bug or a task?

forms.confirmation: Thanks. It is in the backlog.

variables.name: primary_table
variables.describes: Every story, its status, points, owner and whether it is blocked.

variables.name: related_tables
variables.describes: The sprints the stories are committed to.

question.whyItMatters: Isolde asks this at every stand-up.

text.text: One board for the sprint, one backlog for what comes next, and a retrospective after every sprint. Points and velocity add up by themselves.
Say what moved, what is next, and what is blocked.
Tick Blocked on the story the moment it happens.
A story moves to Done only when every box below is true.
Code reviewed by one other person
Automated tests pass on the nightly build
Played through on a console build
Designer has seen it and agreed
No new warnings in the log
Silent writing: went well, to improve, ideas.
Vote on the two items worth discussing.
End with one action and one owner.
